sheet-56.description: Chadwick in 1905, a small resort on the barrier beach between Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic Ocean, drawn at 120 feet to an inch on a single sheet with north toward the upper left. Central Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs the length of the sheet down the middle of the beach, and eight cross avenues, 50 feet wide, run from the railroad to the ocean: Maxson, Pitney, Ocean, Chadwick, Pennsylvania, Camden, New Brunswick and Trenton Avenues. The blocks between them are lettered A to L and divided into numbered lots, most of them still empty; the ocean-front lots east of the blocks are laid out separately. The Penn. & Long Branch Railroad runs along the bay side, with the R.R. station, the Chadwick Hotel and its outbuildings, and a pier or walk into the bay beside them. West of the railroad lie Barnegat Bay, marsh land and the inlet of Riley's Pond, which reaches across the line south of New Brunswick Avenue. Buildings are few and scattered: a summer pavilion in block H, a handful of dwellings, sheds and storage buildings, the Life Saving Station on the ocean side of block A, the Chadwick Chapel south of New Brunswick Avenue, an ice house, a hen house and dwellings along Trenton Avenue, where a boardwalk or walk is drawn east to the beach. A sea wall is marked along the ocean front. The sheet notes a population of 50, no water works, no fire department and prevailing winds from the west and south. The large blocks south of New Brunswick Avenue are not subdivided.
notes: Central Av. is today's Grand Central Avenue; the Penn. & Long Branch R.R. line is today's NJ 35 southbound (West Central Avenue).

None of the 1905 cross avenues survives: the area was replatted later (the Ocean Beach 'Way' streets and Chadwick Beach Island), so modern Pennsylvania, Camden, New Brunswick and Trenton Avenues in Lavallette are different streets.

Placed without street junctions: hand-picked points on Central Av. and the railroad, positioned along the island by fitting the drawn railroad curve to the modern line; the north-south position is uncertain by roughly 50 to 100 m.
Buildings of note: Chadwick Hotel, R.R. station, Life Saving Station, the Chadwick Chapel, a summer pavilion.
Sheet notes: population 50, no water works, no fire department, prevailing wind west and south.

Single sheet 56 of New Jersey Coast vol. 3, Chadwick (barrier island between Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic, today the Chadwick / Ocean Beach area of Toms River Township, north of Lavallette). Scale 120 ft to an inch; north toward the upper left (true north about 11 deg anticlockwise of up). One part. Streets Maxson, Pitney, Ocean, Chadwick, Pennsylvania, Camden, New Brunswick and Trenton Avs. crossing Central Av.; the 1905 cross-street grid was replatted (no old cross street survives), so there is no street junction. Placed from Central Av. = Grand Central Avenue (straight, fits to 0 to 1.7 m) and the Penn. & Long Branch R.R. = NJ 35 southbound on the razed PRR line; the position along the island comes only from matching the drawn railroad curve to the modern line (rail residuals up to 22 m), so it is uncertain by roughly 50 to 100 m. Low confidence.
